subject: octopus
reasoning:
I'm planning a stylized low-poly octopus as a three.js module exporting a THREE.Object3D with meta, aiming for a mantle around 0.4m tall and arms spanning roughly 1.2m, resting with its lowest points touching the floor at y=0.

For construction, I'm thinking of a bulbous SphereGeometry mantle elongated along y, paired with eight tapering arms built from chains of spheres or cylinders curling along the floor with spiral tips, favoring blocky primitive shapes over smooth tube geometries to match the stylized art direction.

I'm sketching proportions too: mantle centered around y=0.32 with roughly 0.22 horizontal radius and 0.4 height, arms spread with a floor-hugging radius around 0.5-0.6m to suggest a realistically-sized octopus without the model becoming oversized.

For each of the eight arms, I'm computing their path by sweeping an angle around the mantle base and integrating a heading that curves more sharply near the tip, producing the natural curling spiral shape, while keeping a slight vertical lift so the arm cylinders sit just above the floor plane.

I'm planning to build each arm from about 14 tapered cylinder segments joined by small spheres at the joints to hide seams, with radius shrinking from 0.075 at the base to 0.012 at the tip, using low-poly geometry for efficiency—roughly 224 meshes total across all arms, plus smaller shapes for suckers.

For the suckers, I'm placing small flattened discs along the upper-facing side of each arm's curve so they're visible from above, rather than tucking them underneath where the floor would hide them, keeping colors pale and the shapes simple to stay well under the mesh budget.

I'm also considering adding a canvas-drawn texture for the mantle's mottled coloring, but I need to guard against document being undefined in non-browser environments, so I'll wrap that texture generation in a typeof check with a plain-color fallback.

For the color palette, I'm settling on a warm coral-orange body with darker reddish-brown spots, pale sucker tones, and large stylized eyes with white sclera, black pupils, and a highlight, positioned low on the front of the mantle. I'm now shaping the mantle itself using a lathe profile to get that bulbous, teardrop dome that narrows down toward where the arms attach.

Working through the lathe points and segment count to keep it low-poly but readable, then figuring out where on that curved surface the eyes should sit—calculating the radius at a given height so the eye spheres poke out naturally from the head rather than floating or sinking in, with the pupils nested just in front of them.

I'm also adding a small funnel-shaped tube under the mantle pointing forward-down, plus considering darker spot details on the surface before moving on to writing a procedural arm generator...

Writing arm generator code...

Working out arm proportions and curvature now — heading direction defined from the +Z axis, with gentle base bending that ramps into a tight spiral toward the tip. I'm sizing the whole creature to roughly a meter across with half-meter arms, tuning segment count and curvature in rad/m so the last 40% of each arm coils about two full turns.

I'm settling on 20 segments per arm at 0.025m each, giving ~160 cylinders and joint spheres across 8 arms plus sucker meshes, keeping the total mesh count comfortably under budget. I'm also making sure the curl stays confined to the ground plane so arms rest naturally on the floor, varying curl direction per arm so they don't all spiral the same way and collide with the mantle or each other.

Checking spacing: with 8 arms radiating at 45° intervals and extending ~0.5m, adjacent arms stay roughly 0.38m apart at full extension, which is enough room even with tip curls spiraling outward at a small radius. I'm tapering the arm radius down near the tip so the curls look natural, and jittering each arm's base heading slightly so they don't look perfectly symmetric, while keeping the arm's vertical position tied to ground contact.

Rather than fighting the lift/slope math precisely to keep every cylinder segment above the floor, the simpler fix is to just compute a bounding box of the final assembled object and translate the whole thing so its minimum y sits at zero -- that way any slight dips from sloped segments get absorbed automatically.

For the limb segments, I'm planning sphere joints at each point with tapered cylinders connecting them, orienting each cylinder with a quaternion from the up vector to the segment direction, and giving each segment its own geometry to handle the taper rather than trying to share geometries.

Now I'm figuring out sucker placement along the arm — adding them at every other joint, offset outward and slightly upward from the arm's surface using cross products of the direction and up vectors to get lateral positioning, so they sit naturally along both sides of the limb.

I realize the mesh count could balloon if I create individual sucker meshes, so I'm switching to InstancedMesh for all the suckers, using a dummy Object3D to compose each transform matrix before calling setMatrixAt — this keeps performance in check while still letting each sucker have its own position and scale. I'm also considering adding a canvas texture for mantle spots and arm patterning.

I'm also working out positioning: the mantle needs to sit low enough that its base overlaps where the arms attach, so I'm estimating the vertical offsets and final height so everything aligns properly once I shift the whole model to rest on the floor.

Working out how the arm bases blend into the mantle's underside geometrically — figuring out the lift function so arms curve upward into the mantle at a reasonable radius without visually detaching from the body.

I'm settling on lifting the mantle group by 0.12 so its base hovers just above the arm floor, letting the arms rise into it, and then placing eye positions on the mantle surface by checking that the radial distance from center roughly matches the mantle's local radius at that height.

For the eyes, I'm going with a layered design: a white sphere base, a smaller dark pupil offset outward, and a tiny highlight sphere for gleam, plus a torus "lid" ring oriented along the outward normal direction to frame each eye with a darker reddish-brown color. I'm also planning a small funnel cone near the mantle's front-bottom to complete the squid-like features.

I'm deciding to keep the octopus as the sole subject, skipping any additional rocks or seabed props, and considering slight color variation at the arm tips with a paler ring for visual interest.
